data.title: How to Web 2026 brings tech leaders and investors to Bucharest to discuss AI and startup growth
data.description: How to Web Conference 2026, a leading startup and technology conference in Eastern Europe held annually, brought together technology leaders, investors, startup founders, business professionals, and representatives of European institutions and the public sector in Bucharest from October 6 to 8. With the theme “What will you build when you can build anything?” the event covered product strategy, leadership, and the role of investment in building globally competitive companies. Among the speakers, Teodora Mușatoiu (OpenAI) and Aleodor Tabarcea (Stripe Romania) addressed the changes AI is bringing to product development and team organization, as well as the challenges of adopting new technologies. The agenda also featured the Bitdefender Academy Season Finale, a session dedicated to training the next generation of technology product development specialists. Nesrine Changuel, former product leader at Google and Spotify, spoke about the importance of the emotional connection between users and products, while Sara Maldon (Inflect, formerly Make) discussed measuring the impact of AI investments. Thomas Kolarik, VP IT & Operations at BCR, and Zoltan Vardy, Founder & Sales and GTM Advisor at The Launch Code, discussed demand for technology in Eastern Europe and the role companies can play in accelerating its adoption. Similarly, Michał Kramarz (Google Cloud) presented the challenges of international expansion and the factors that contribute to scaling startups and AI-driven initiatives. Financing businesses with a social impact was addressed during the MARC Impact Programme session, “Somebody has to get paid to fix this,” where entrepreneurs and investors discussed developing sustainable business models and attracting capital. Finally, the impact of technology on society was another topic discussed at How to Web 2026 by Bogdan Iordache, General Partner at Underline Ventures, Radu Magdin, and Dragoș Stanca. During the event, Hack for Facts, an initiative by AmpliFY ONG and Ethical Media Alliance, brought together journalists, technology professionals, and representatives of civil society organizations to explore the use of digital tools in the public interest, from supporting investigative journalism to developing sustainable models for independent journalism. Discussions on Europe’s competitiveness also focused on public policies and measures to support the development of the tech industry. During the “Bytes & Bills” session, representatives of European institutions, Romania’s public sector, and the private sector discussed the measures needed to support startup growth. Speakers included Marc Lemaître, Director-General for Research and Innovation at the European Commission, Camelia Drăgoi (European Investment Fund), Ervin Luga (EBRD Venture Capital), and Irina Avram (Romanian Ministry of Finance). The agenda also featured discussions on technological sovereignty and defense technologies with both civilian and military applications. How to Web 2026 brought representatives of the international venture capital community to Bucharest. Investors Summit, organized on October 6, brought together more than 200 investors and representatives of over 80 funds and institutions. The Spotlight competition, also part of the conference, provided 20 participating early-stage startups with mentoring, visibility, and access to investors. This year’s winner, AISafe Labs, a Romanian cybersecurity startup, secured an investment commitment from TechAngels, with the financing terms to be negotiated between the parties.

data.title: Cushman & Wakefield Echinox: Romania delivered more than 636,000 new homes over past decade, above several European markets
data.description: More than 636,000 homes were completed in Romania between 2016 and 2025, equivalent to almost 33 new homes per 1,000 inhabitants, according to an analysis by Cushman & Wakefield Echinox based on housing completion data compiled for the 2016-2025 period. This compared with 33.6 in Germany, 34.4 in Slovakia and 31.5 in Czechia. Residential construction intensity was considerably higher in markets such as Poland, with 55.2 homes/1,000 inhabitants, France (52.8), Finland (62.8) and the Netherlands (39). The figures placed Romania broadly in the middle of the 21 European markets included in the analysis, close to Germany, Slovakia and Czechia, while significantly ahead of Hungary, Spain and Portugal in terms of housing deliveries relative to population. At the other end of the spectrum, the indicator stood at 26.2 in Bulgaria, 23.9 in the United Kingdom, 18.2 in Hungary, 16.4 in Spain and 15.7 in Portugal. In absolute terms, 636,310 homes were completed in Romania between 2016 and 2025 according to the National Institute of Statistics. Annual deliveries increased from 52,200 units in 2016 to a peak of 73,300 units in 2022. Subsequently, the market entered a downward phase, with completions falling to 71,000 homes in 2023, 61,000 in 2024, and 59,000 in 2025. Consequently, the 2025 volume was ~19.5% below the 2022 peak, but still 13% above the 2016 level. The differences between Romania’s main cities (those with a population exceeding 100,000 inhabitants) were even more pronounced. Bucharest was by far the country’s largest residential market in absolute terms, with 93,850 homes completed between 2016 and 2025, compared with 25,200 in Cluj-Napoca and 22,300 in Brasov. However, a different picture emerged when deliveries are connected to the population size. Brasov leads the major cities included in the analysis, with 94 completed homes/1,000 inhabitants during the decade, followed by Cluj-Napoca with 88. Sibiu recorded 61.8 homes/1,000 inhabitants, Oradea 58.1, while Bucharest reached 52.5. Timisoara came close to the capital city, with 50.1 homes/1,000 inhabitants. Below these levels were Constanta, at 43.2 homes/1,000 inhabitants, Iasi (38.8), Targu Mures (36.1), and Craiova at 32.2. At the lower end of the ranking, Ploiesti recorded just 8.1 completed homes/1,000 inhabitants, Braila 10.2, Baia Mare 11, and Buzau 11.5 during the analyzed period. The recent figures also suggested that Romania has moved beyond the exceptionally strong residential delivery cycle recorded at the beginning of this decade. Following the peak of 73,300 completed homes in 2022, national deliveries decreased by 3.2% in 2023, by a further 14.1% in 2024 and by 3.1% in 2025. The slowdown was visible in most of the country’s major residential markets. Bucharest delivered 9,361 homes in 2025, compared with a decade-high 13,834 units in 2023, representing a decline of ~32% from that peak. Despite the correction, Bucharest’s 2025 volume remained approximately 144% above the 3,838 homes completed in 2016. The adjustment has been considerably sharper in some regional centers. Cluj-Napoca recorded 957 completions in 2025, compared with 4,175 at its 2019 peak, while Brasov delivered 1,283 homes versus a peak of 3,098 in 2020. Timisoara reached 793 completions in 2025, compared with 1,787 in 2021, and Iasi recorded 780, compared with 1,908 in 2019.

data.title: Bucharest’s Living Museum opens without a building or entrance fee
data.description: The new Living Museum opened in October with a permanent collection of 68 places. Bucharest residents can discover and visit them for free using the map available on muzeulviu.ro . The museum is meant to offer a new perspective on the capital, starting from places that are part of the city’s everyday life. The collection includes a wide range of projects from gardens, meadows, and urban habitats to spaces reclaimed for the community and initiatives through which resources are reused. The exhibits in Bucharest’s Living Museum are not kept in display cases but outdoors, where they grow, change with the seasons, and need care. Bucharest residents can follow the transformations of each project, and at some of them they can even lend a hand through planting, gardening, or building shelters for birds, hedgehogs, and insects. The digital map available on muzeulviu.ro serves as the museum’s catalog: it provides information about each project and suggests recommended thematic routes for a few hours or a full day of exploration in the city. “Bucharest’s Living Museum is a collection that showcases precisely this urban energy, without being a museum in the institutional sense, but rather an invitation to look at the city itself as a museum. The 68 ‘living exhibits’ show what happens when Bucharest residents are determined to care for their environment and make the city a better place to live through their own efforts. It is an open museum that celebrates not relics in display cases, but every project that proves Bucharest is changing for the better,” says Alina Kasprovschi, executive director of Bucharest Community Foundation. The 68 projects included in the collection of Bucharest’s Living Museum are projects supported by Bucharest Community Foundation and ING Bank Romania through the Environmental Platform for Bucharest. The program connects research into environmental problems with the funding of solutions and the collaboration needed to implement them, bringing together those who can contribute to these interventions, from organizations and civic groups to specialists, academia, companies, and public administration. The priorities of the Environmental Platform for Bucharest are based on research into the state of the environment in Bucharest. Data on air quality, urban nature, climate change, waste management, and mobility help identify the city’s problems and establish priorities. Funding totaling nearly RON 22 million to date supports the development and continuation of initiatives, while collaboration connects resources, expertise, and the communities involved. The support provided covers interventions at different scales, from large-scale projects dedicated to conserving urban nature and regenerating public spaces to initiatives developed by communities at the neighborhood level. These address different needs but share a focus on places and the people who use them, and Bucharest’s Living Museum connects them in a network accessible to Bucharest residents. Until the end of November 2026, Bucharest’s Living Museum hosts weekly activities and gatherings at selected locations in the active collection. The updated calendar, access information, and participation details are available on muzeulviu.ro. On the weekend of October 17-18, the program brings Bucharest residents into the heart of the collection through workshops for children, biodiversity exploration, and activities in community gardens.

data.title: Update: Greenpeace Romania protests at IKEA over alleged links to Carpathian forest logging
data.description: Greenpeace Romania activists staged a peaceful protest outside the IKEA Pallady store in Bucharest on Tuesday, October 13, placing sawdust and sections of tree trunks at the entrance. The demonstration coincided with the release of an investigation into logging in Romania’s Poiana Ruscă Mountains and a separate Greenpeace Nordic report on IKEA’s forest policies. Greenpeace said its investigation also focused on Plot 37 in the Natura 2000 site ROSCI0219, a centuries-old forest that had appeared on a list of areas proposed for strict protection under the EU’s 10% biodiversity target. According to the organization, the forest was clear-cut before receiving protected status and subsequently disappeared from the map of areas eligible for strict protection. Greenpeace also alleged that official timber transport records showed the wood reached an intermediary storage facility that supplies a factory operated by a key IKEA supplier. “The case in Rusca Montană provides clear evidence from the field: a forest proposed for strict protection was clear-cut before the law could save it, and the timber most likely went to factories producing furniture for IKEA,” said Valentin Sălăgeanu, forests and biodiversity campaign coordinator at Greenpeace Romania. Greenpeace said roads had been cut into steep slopes, a stream bed had been used to transport timber, and no habitat trees or deadwood remained on the site. The organization called on IKEA to stop sourcing wood from forests proposed for strict protection and remove an exception in its IWAY sourcing rules that allows purchases from high-conservation-value forests when they are certified by the Forest Stewardship Council. It also urged the Romanian government and Environment Ministry to impose a moratorium on logging across 1.9 million hectares mapped for possible strict protection under the country’s National Recovery and Resilience Plan. The non-profit said IKEA received the investigation before publication and disputed its conclusions. Inter IKEA Group said the logging in Plot 37 had been legally authorized under an approved forest management plan in a Natura 2000 area and described the photographic evidence as an unrepresentative snapshot. Moreover, the company said it had appointed experts to monitor the site’s regeneration alongside the FSC and local authorities. Greenpeace argued that IKEA’s response did not address the operational issues documented at the site and said reliance on legal compliance and certification was insufficient to protect forests with high biodiversity value.

data.title: Romania to receive C-130H Hercules aircraft from the US
data.description: Romania will receive a C-130H Hercules aircraft from the United States government on Wednesday, October 14, the Defense Ministry (MApN) announced, as reported by News.ro . A handover ceremony will take place at the Romanian Air Force’s 90th Airlift Base in Otopeni. Defense minister Radu Miruță and US ambassador to Romania Darryl Nirenberg are expected to attend the event. The aircraft is being transferred free of charge through the Excess Defense Articles (EDA) program, which allows eligible countries to receive surplus US military equipment, the ministry explained. “Romania has benefited from the EDA program since 1996, when C-130B aircraft were integrated into the Romanian Air Force’s transport fleet. This is the eighth aircraft of this type to enter service with the Romanian Armed Forces through the EDA program,” reads the MApN statement . The C-130H can conduct air transport, medical evacuation, humanitarian assistance, and disaster relief missions. The ministry said the transfer also highlights the defense cooperation developed during nearly three decades of strategic partnership between Romania and the United States.

data.title: Romania’s Forestry Guard launches digital platform for complaints
data.description: The National Forestry Guard launched a new digital platform on Monday, October 12, through which citizens can submit and track complaints regarding illegal tree cutting and other irregularities in forests, as well as consult a map showing the locations of inspections carried out by inspectors, the damage identified, and the penalties imposed. The new application, presented by interim environment minister Diana Buzoianu and National Forestry Guard general inspector Florin George Gârbacea at a press conference, aims both to increase the transparency of inspections and to change the way complaints regarding violations of forestry legislation are registered, resolved, and evaluated. The application includes information on the historical boundaries of forest land, dating back to 1990, data from forestry management plans, and a system for evaluating the performance of the nine regional forestry guards. It was developed within the institution, without contracting external programming services. The minister explained that, until now, citizens submitting petitions regarding possible illegal tree cutting had no tool available to track what happened to their complaints. Inspections could take months, and petitioners had to wait for the institution’s response without being able to access information about the progress of the inspection or its results. Through the new platform, each complaint submitted online will automatically receive a registration number, which will be sent to the petitioner by email. They will subsequently be able to check the status of the petition, the time elapsed since registration, whether an inspection has been carried out, and the conclusions of the checks. The system includes a timeline of the complaint resolution process, from registration to the communication of the response. https://www.facebook.com/DianaBuzoianu/videos/968539316296158/ Moreover, the electronic form allows for documents that can help inspectors identify the location and nature of the reported irregularities to be attached. Citizens are encouraged to submit photographs with GPS location data, geographical coordinates, cadastral documents, and other relevant materials. Gârbacea explained that this information can be particularly important when unmarked tree stumps, suspicious tree cutting, or interventions in areas where the boundaries of forest land are unclear are reported. The application also tracks compliance with deadlines for resolving petitions. The general inspector stated that after a complaint is registered, the system automatically calculates the 30-day response deadline. In the internal module, petitions that are still within the deadline are marked in green, while those that have exceeded it are highlighted in red. Depending on the complexity of the inspections, the deadline may also be extended in accordance with the law. The platform includes an interactive map displaying Forestry Guard inspections and their geographical locations. Users can select an inspection to view a summary of the checks and a report containing their results, including whether violations of the law were identified and whether fines were imposed. Public information within the form is anonymized, meaning that the names of people who filed complaints will not be displayed, and inspection reports will not include identifying information about the companies inspected. According to the general inspector, this measure is important because some citizens hesitate to report irregularities for fear that their identities might become known. The platform is not limited to inspections initiated following complaints. According to the Forestry Guard’s leadership, all inspections carried out by inspectors will eventually be entered into the system, regardless of whether they were prompted by citizens’ petitions or initiated by the institution itself. At the time of the launch, however, not all inspections had been uploaded to the application. During the demonstration, Gârbacea explained that more inspections had been carried out than were visible on the map, and that some features, including those for mobile phone use, were still under development. The environment minister stated that people who have filed complaints can request to participate in inspections carried out by forestry inspectors. The measure was not introduced through the new platform but through a decision by the general inspector that had already been in effect for several weeks. Buzoianu explained that there had been complaints that inspectors arriving at a site did not check the exact locations indicated in the reports. According to her, the presence of petitioners can help identify the exact locations where possible illegal activities have been observed and prevent situations in which inspections are carried out in an area other than the one reported. The environment minister also presented data on the Forestry Guard’s activity during the first six months of 2026, compared with the same period in 2025. In this period, the number of inspections increased by approximately 9–10%, while the value of the damage identified reached RON 3.85 million, compared with RON 1.34 million in the first half of last year. Buzoianu stated that these results were achieved with the same number of inspectors and the same inspection tools, noting that the difference was related to the prioritization of checks and changes in the leadership of some regional units. The volume of illegally cut timber identified by inspectors also increased, from approximately 2,700–2,800 cubic meters in the first six months of 2025 to around 6,000 cubic meters in the same period of 2026.

According to the general inspector, this measure is important because some citizens hesitate to report irregularities for fear that their identities might become known. The platform is not limited to inspections initiated following complaints. According to the Forestry Guard’s leadership, all inspections carried out by inspectors will eventually be entered into the system, regardless of whether they were prompted by citizens’ petitions or initiated by the institution itself. At the time of the launch, however, not all inspections had been uploaded to the application. During the demonstration, Gârbacea explained that more inspections had been carried out than were visible on the map, and that some features, including those for mobile phone use, were still under development. The environment minister stated that people who have filed complaints can request to participate in inspections carried out by forestry inspectors. The measure was not introduced through the new platform but through a decision by the general inspector that had already been in effect for several weeks. Buzoianu explained that there had been complaints that inspectors arriving at a site did not check the exact locations indicated in the reports. According to her, the presence of petitioners can help identify the exact locations where possible illegal activities have been observed and prevent situations in which inspections are carried out in an area other than the one reported. The environment minister also presented data on the Forestry Guard’s activity during the first six months of 2026, compared with the same period in 2025. In this period, the number of inspections increased by approximately 9–10%, while the value of the damage identified reached RON 3.85 million, compared with RON 1.34 million in the first half of last year. Buzoianu stated that these results were achieved with the same number of inspectors and the same inspection tools, noting that the difference was related to the prioritization of checks and changes in the leadership of some regional units. The volume of illegally cut timber identified by inspectors also increased, from approximately 2,700–2,800 cubic meters in the first six months of 2025 to around 6,000 cubic meters in the same period of 2026.

data.title: Romania’s Electric Castle announces dates for 2027 edition
data.description: The 13th edition of Romania’s Electric Castle festival will take place from July 15 to 18, 2027, organizers announced. Hundreds of artists and activities are expected, with the lineup to be announced at a later date. General-access passes are already on sale, with prices starting at EUR 159 plus fees. “On the program: something new - hundreds of artists and experiences; something old - a centuries-old castle with stories waiting to be continued; and something blue - the July sky, with spectacular sunsets competing with the main-stage shows,” organizers said, as quoted by News.ro . The 2026 edition of Electric Castle attracted 272,000 attendees. More than 20 full concerts from this year’s festival are also being released on its YouTube channel, including performances by Teddy Swims, Archive, Dub Pistols, Kneecap, and House of Protection. Details about the 2027 edition and tickets are available on the event’s website.

data.title: Swiss manufacturer VAT expands factory in Romania’s Arad
data.description: VAT Romania, a subsidiary of Switzerland-based VAT Group, announced that it is expanding its factory in Arad by approximately 800 sqm, just over a year after the production facility opened. The expansion is intended to support a gradual shift from components and subassemblies to finished products shipped directly to customers. The construction is scheduled for completion by mid-December 2026. The additional space will include a shipping area for finished products, more storage capacity, and facilities supporting final assembly. The component production capacity at the Arad plant increased by approximately 30% in 2026, with another expansion planned for 2027. VAT is also investing in local final-product assembly, automation, and digitalization. “The development of the Arad factory confirms the potential we identified in Romania when we decided to build the new production facility,” said Alin Crețu, general manager of VAT Romania. “Demand from the semiconductor industry and the capabilities we have developed here allow us to continue this evolution and gradually introduce new products and production processes in Arad.” The factory currently produces components and products for the semiconductor, display, and photovoltaic industries, as well as scientific instruments and particle accelerator applications. The production involves high-precision machining processes such as milling and turning. The resulting components are used in systems where precision, purity, and airtightness are required for vacuum-based manufacturing, the company said. “Romania has strengthened its important role in our global production network, supplying components and assemblies used in some of the world’s most advanced technologies,” VAT Group CEO Urs Gantner stated. The Romanian subsidiary had more than 500 employees at the end of the first half of 2026, an increase of over 50% from the end of 2025. The number of employees directly involved in production rose by more than 70% over the same period, and the company expects further workforce growth in 2027. All products manufactured at the Arad plant are exported, currently to European markets. VAT has operated in Romania since 2001, initially through a company called SYSMEC, which was fully integrated into VAT Group in 2008 and renamed VAT Romania in 2019. Arad is now one of the group’s three main operational centers worldwide, alongside facilities in Switzerland and Malaysia. The factory opened in June 2025 and includes more than 3,000 sqm of cleanroom production space. VAT Group, which specializes in high-performance vacuum valves, reported net sales of CHF 1.07 billion in 2025 and employs nearly 4,000 people worldwide.

data.title: IMF forecasts 0.5% recession in Romania in 2026, slower recovery in 2027
data.description: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) sharply revised its estimates for Romania’s economy this month, forecasting a recession this year and a slower recovery in 2027 than initially expected, according to data analyzed by Profit.ro . Romania’s economy is now expected to shrink by 0.5% in 2026, compared with growth of 0.7% estimated in the spring. The new estimate is in line with that of the World Bank , which was also recently revised downward. At the same time, the IMF anticipated economic growth of 2.2% in 2027 for Romania, compared with the previously estimated 2.5% increase. The current account deficit is similarly expected to widen to 7% of GDP in 2026, up 0.2% from the previous forecast, and narrow to 6.7% of GDP next year. Labor market conditions are also expected to deteriorate, with the unemployment rate forecast to rise to 6.5% this year, compared with 6.1% in 2025 and the previously projected rate of 6% forecast by the IMF. Globally, the IMF has kept its forecast for growth of 3.1% in 2026 unchanged, noting the positive demand-side effect of investments in artificial intelligence and related infrastructure and hardware equipment. Global economic growth is expected to accelerate to 3.4% in 2027, very close to the 3.5% increase recorded last year. However, the IMF warns that the apparent stability of the global economy actually masks a redistribution of growth among countries, depending on their exposure to the supply shock caused by wars and the intensity of demand associated with artificial intelligence. “Currently, 32 economies generate 95% of global growth, compared with 54 economies in April, while downward revisions have become more frequent, affecting approximately 47% of economies,” according to the report . Geopolitical risks, particularly in the Middle East, will continue to impact trade relations and economic activity, according to the IMF. The negative supply shock generated by the war is spreading through the economy via higher and more volatile energy prices, as well as their impact on inflation dynamics. “So far, the private sector appears to have adapted well to the geopolitical shocks caused by direct conflicts and trade disputes. However, as short periods of calm alternate with waves of attacks in a prolonged and protracted conflict, some of the adjustment mechanisms that protected the global economy in the initial phase — based on the assumption that hostilities would be short-lived — are narrowing, and the risk of higher economic costs is becoming increasingly evident,” the report also stated.

data.title: Two Nights Without Missile Warnings – Zelensky Raises Alarm as Trump Denies Intelligence Cutoff
data.description: Ukraine received no advance allied warnings during Russian ballistic missile attacks on Kyiv on Oct. 12 and 13. Zelensky sounded the alarm without naming the country responsible. The failures followed an Axios report that US officials threatened to suspend intelligence sharing over Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries. Trump denied any cutoff, while his new press secretary said she would look into the matter.

data.title: 12 Senators Sign Bipartisan Letter Urging Trump to Rescind Russian Diesel Deal
data.description:
Twelve US senators – six Republicans and six Democrats – signed a joint
letter urging US President Donald Trump on Monday to rescind his Oct. 9 diesel arrangement with Russian President Vladimir Putin. They called it a betrayal of Ukraine and demanded the president to enforce the new Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, signed by Trump just three weeks before striking the deal with the Kremlin leader.

data.title: Phantom Defense Buys Developer of KARAKURT Drone Net Launchers
data.description: Ukrainian counter-drone company Phantom Defense has acquired the full business and team behind KARAKURT net launchers, which military units have used in more than 50,000 kits over six months. It also introduced MANGAL, an AI-guided system with six net launchers and a one-second response time, built to protect vehicles, positions and unmanned ground vehicles.

data.title: Ireland Aims to Open All Remaining EU Accession Clusters for Ukraine by Year-End
data.description: The EU successfully opened Ukraine’s Clusters 2 and 3; the internal market, and competitiveness and inclusive growth on Tuesday, Oct. 13, a day after all 27 member states unanimously agreed to open them as Ukraine adopted a minority education law that Hungary had demanded in exchange for lifting its veto on the EU bid. Ireland’s minister of state for European affairs and defense said Ireland’s EU presidency aims to open the remaining two clusters by the end of 2026.

data.title: Russian Drone Attack Kills 1, Injures 2 in Pavlohrad
data.description: Russian forces launched a drone attack on Pavlohrad, killing one person and injuring two on Tuesday, Oct. 13. According to Head of the Dnipropetrovsk Regional Military Administration Oleksandr Hanzha, Russian drones and artillery struck four districts of the region nearly 40 times, injuring two people in the Nikopol area and causing fires in Dnipro earlier in the afternoon. The overall number of casualties in the region on Tuesday is one dead, five wounded.

data.description: Ukraine has pushed about $876 million of spending to year-end, left $1.03 billion in payments unprocessed and suspended $404 million in VAT refunds, Finance Minister Serhiy Marchenko told the Verkhovna Rada. data.title: DSP o Maquiavélico Ganancioso
data.description: Guineenses, mais uma vez, venho para vos alertar sobre o perigo que Domingos Simões Pereira representa para a Guiné-Bissau. Faço esse alerta a todos os guineenses sem exceção que se encontre no país ou no estrangeiro, ao PAIGC em especial e na pessoa do Cipriano Cassamá em concreto. Alerta esse sobre o verdadeiro DSP, o verdadeiro espírito que move esse sujeito, o qual alguns ainda continuam a acreditar para não dizer adorar. Domingos Simões Pereira é um manipulador, um verdadeiro chantagista e calculista provavelmente, tipo de comportamento que ultrapassa o nível de psicopata. U m ambicioso desmedido, um verdadeiro criminoso que sabe como e quando cometer o crime. Ele jamais coabitaria não só com JOMAV, assim como com qualquer presidente que seria eleito, a não ser o que ele apoiou disfarçadamente. Isto porque ele tem sua própria agenda, e o PAIGC é simplesmente uma plataforma para sua concretização. DSP jamais coabitaria com JOMAV porque o seu candidato preferido era o Paulo Gomes e sempre será, o qual juntamente com Tchitchi vão delineando mecanismo de modo a serem os novos donos da Guiné-Bissau. Segundo eles este é um processo a médio prazo, e é preciso coragem e paciência para concretiza-lo. Ganhar o congresso não importa em que circunstância e ter novamente o partido na mão, é uma fase concluída em proveito deles, enquanto verdadeiros militantes do PAIGC estão a bater palmas. Depois dessa eleição legislativa, não importa o resultado, o Cipriano Cassama que se prepare a mala ou fica de bico fechado, pois o candidato preferido para o partido será o Paulo Gomes, e esse sim deve ter a voz dentro do partido. DSP é um ambicioso desmedido, nunca teve consideração por ninguém, JOMAV muito menos, o sujeito é um maquiavélico nato, Cipriano Casama será descartado quando menos esperar podes tomar a nota. Guineenses, falar do Paulo Gomes e Tchitchi é falar do MCCI e demais outras organizações e personalidades camufladas no nosso país. Esses dois indivíduos são os principais financiadores do MCCI e demais outras personalidades boca de aluguel na cidade de Bissau. O MCCI, Milícia idealizado por JBV e DSP, agora financiado e dirigido por "futuro triângulo do poder" ou seja, "DSP, Paulo Gomes e Tchitchi", têm 3 principais objectivos: 1º Perturbar a ordem pública em nome da cidadania, difamar e tentar descredibilizar qualquer que seja organizações ou indivíduos não alinhados ao triângulo, de modo a suportar suas caminhadas na busca do poder. 2º Caso se concretize o objectivo do triângulo, o papel da Milícia do MCCI passará a ser de vigilância constante a todos os adversários de modo a garantir falsa paz social e o poder de controlo. 3º Tentar ganhar credibilidade junto das organizações internacionais e regionais, através de suas visitas e actividades de fachada, para quando houver as tais actividades de perturbações de ordem pública, poderem ganhar notoriedade. Mas isso não deve preocupar ninguém, pois estão bem identificados e bem caçados, dentro e fora da Guiné-Bissau. Não tenho nada contra ninguém, mas quem continuar a perturbar verdadeira paz social dos guineenses em troca de benefícios como sempre foi nos últimos anos dessa crise, e que sempre tenho tolerado, então que fique claro "estou firme e determinado para tudo e todos". Para finalizar, gostaria de vos deixar uma reflexão com a seguinte frase: " Domingos Simões Pereira é um perigo grave para o futuro do país ". Isto porque publicar aqui tudo que é necessário para provar ou sustentar a razão dessa frase, só pode agravar ainda mais a paz social que tanto necessitamos. Chega, chega não podemos continuar a viver nessa turbulência vida toda, meus irmãos guineenses, não é saudável, é tóxico, não é justo para um povo que tanto sofreu. António Aly Silva » aaly.silva@gmail.com » aaly_silva@hotmail.com » Tel. (+245) 668 31 13

data.title: APANHA-SE MAIS DEPRESSA UM MENTIROSO QUE UM COXO!
data.description:
DSP através da sua equipa de "Lambe-Botas" está cavando cada vez mais a sua própria cova, adiantando cada vez mais o seu fim. Somente alguns acreditavam que foi ele quem estava por trás do "Progresso Nacional" o blog onde começou toda essa história de Mentiras, Calunias, Difamações, Ameaças e tantos outros agressões tóxicas ao espírito humano, a todos os que não estão do seu lado e cujo o único objectivo, era ser chamado de rei dos réis da Guiné. Comandou o Progresso Nacional assim como Bin Laden comandou a Al-Qaeda e acabou por fracassar. Pensou, repensou e resolveu voltar novamente ainda com mais TERROR e está a comandar o Guiné Puro tentando levar toda a nação ao abismo assim como o ISIS quer levar a humanidade. Camaradas, Guiné Puro assim como o falecido Progresso Nacional é o reflexo do espirito de DSP, alí é possivel ver tudo e quanto o sujeito é baixo. DSP é um hipócrita e um anarquista moderno. "ACHAS QUE AS NOSSAS MARCHAS SÃO RESULTADO DE VENDAS E COMPRAS?!" essa foi uma das frases da recente publicação que mostram por quem e para que fim, é dirigido o Guiné Puro ou melhor o blog do terror como podem ver já a seguir. Demonstraram mais uma vez claramente que o "MCCI" pertence a DPS, pois uma publicação dessa no próprio blog do ganancioso só pode ser das duas uma: "Boca capli elis ou Foronta passanta e dicidi ca sucundi rostu". Camaradas, Domingos Simões Pereira afundou seu próprio barco devido a sua ganância e complexo de superioridade. "I pirigu pa i faladu ba cuma, el i unicu alguim cu bai escola na Guiné" seu ultimo desejo é "afundar com todos, inclusive o PAIGC". __________PARA A VOSSA CONFIRMAÇÃO, AQUI ESTÁ A PUBLICAÇÃO_________ MARCOS GALINA BARBOSA VAI PERCEBER QUE METEU COM GENTE
PERSISTENTE. BÔ DISSAL I NA BIN FASSI PASSSAÇÃO LI. tUDO PUBLICAÇÕES KU I FASSI
I NA RESP+UNDI PAREL. NIN IKANA SEDU DIDIA. NONA VINGAL MANERA KU NÓ PUDI. JÁ
TEMOS ALGUÉM NO AEROPORTO PARA NOS INFOMAR O DIA EM QUE EL CHEGAR. INVENTOU
AGRESSÃO E NESTE MOMENTO ESTÁ EM QUELUZ EM PORTUGAL. FILHO DA PUTA. MENTIROSO
COMO OS TEUS PATRÕES OS SUJOS JOMAV E BRAIMA CAMARÁ. MARCOS GALINA, BU NA
ARREPENDI. PERA BU DJUBI. ACHAS QUE AS NOSSAS MARCHAS SÃO RESULTADO DE VENDAS E
COMPRAS?! VAMOS PROVAR DEPOIS. FIDJU DI BALETA Olá a todos, ainda bem que descobriram
que o Pirata informático- hackec é o Marcos Galina Barbosa, Eng. Informático.
Tentei várias vezes avisar o Ticha Aly Silva mas ele não respondeu e nem deu
importância julgo eu. No tempo da campanha para a liderança do Paigc, este
indivíduo era um fervoroso apoiante do Bá Quecuto no Facebook e a técnica que
usava era o envio de Phishing aos apoiantes do Dsp, recolhia informações
pessoais das pessoas que posteriormente eram expostas no Blog do Doka. Tentou
comigo mas não resultou. Tenham cuidado com este sujeito que está nas mãos de
B. Camara. Outra coisa, gostaria de conhecer a vossa página no Fecebook. Estamos Juntos. AC Nota GP: Até jovens inocentes,
Lesmes, Masta Tito e demais outros, os tais vendidos e comprados foram as tuas
vítimas. teu filho da puta que o bandido de Baciro Djá trouxe para Bissau para funções no aparelho de Estado e dizes que outros recebem favores.
Desde quando é que és mais honesto ou
mais competentes que os outros? Pagas e até pode ser com a tua vida para
perceberes as irresponsabilidades
dos teus actos. Publicada por O

data.title: DSP, UM PERIGO GRAVE PARA FUTURO DO PAÍS
data.description: Os meios de comunicação também são as formas de manipulação mais utilizadas pelos poderes políticos, dado o seu impacto social. As informações são manipuladas não apenas tendo em vista omitir factos relevantes, mas também distorcer o conteúdo da informação veiculada, produzir ou forjar a opinião pública, de modo que a mesma se ajuste às ideias dos gananciosos. A única forma dos cidadãos evitarem cair nestes processos de manipulação é tornarem-se mais vigilantes em relação às instituições democráticas e aos órgãos de informação, adoptando uma atitude de permanente reflexão crítica sobre a informação que lhes é fornecida. Na Guiné-Bissau, nos últimos anos, cresceu exponencialmente o número de pessoas mediocres, pessoas sem escrúpulos ligadas à produção de rádios e outros meios de comunicação com influencia na nossa sociedade, gente que apesar da sua enorme influência na sociedade, trabalha na mais completa impunidade e sem qualquer controlo ético/democrático. Obcecado pelo poder, ciente da dificuldade do povo guineense em avaliar informações, ciente do poder dos instrumentos de comunicação, Domingos Simões Pereira (DSP) nunca menosprezou esses instrumentos para atingir seu objectivo, sempre usou-os de forma desonesta como agora está a fazer tudo por tudo para manter no controlo desses veicúlos, mesmo que isso custe a vida dos outros. Governou na corrupção, no nepotismo e no desvios de somas astronómicas do dinheiro de povo, que muito serviria para investimentos na saúde, educação e outros serviços publicos, para beneficiar familiares e amigos. Finge que preocupa com os problemas do país, mas só engana o povo honesto, humilde e trabalhador que infelizmente sofre muito, não sei até quando, devido a sua paciência e tolerância aos governantes como DSP, criminoso travestido em politico que vive na custa de povo e acima de tudo ainda fa-lo refem do próprio suor. Roubou e decepcionou tanto não só aos guineenses assim como a comunidade internacional que sempre acreditou que o sujeito era ideal para ajudar esse povo a sair do ciclo de sofrimento que parece infinito. Foi demitido, não conformou e está a fazer tudo na medida do possível para continuar a complicar a vida dos guineenses. Razão disso é que depois de perder a batalha nos meios de comunicações mais modernos nomeadamente os blogues onde investiu grandes somas do dinheiro de povo, para fazer a lavagem cerebral dos menos instruídos e não só. Fugiu do facebook onde sempre frequentava e comunicava com todos tentado passar a mensagem de um politico moderno e aberto a diálogo/opiniões, mas que afinal era simplesmente um falso modernista. Caiu a mascara e já não consegue enganar ninguem, pois a sua credibilidade está abaixo de zero, para não dizer outra coisa. Camaradas, para conhecimento geral, com o dinheiro roubado que custou suor de povo guineense, DSP decidiu avançar com um outro novo plano maquiavelico, para criar a sua própria estação de rádio. Documento António Aly Silva » aaly.silva@gmail.com » aaly_silva@hotmail.com » Tel. (+245) 668 31 13

data.title: DSP não respeita os antigos combatentes e sempre usou e abusou desses camaradas. Prova disso é que continuou a governar mesmo já com Carlos Correia como primeiro ministro. Usou até o cadáver de Carmem Perreira para promover sua imagem, pois é sabido que a malograda como sendo antigo combatente e membro do PAIGC o corpo só deveria passar por ANP e sede do partido e nunca na Primatura como aconteceu, e por cima de tudo com indivíduos alí barricados por vontade própria vandalizando instituição do estado o que demonstra uma clara promoção ao anarquismo. Não respeitou nem o Pai da Nação(ALC), nem o PR quanto mais o formalismo de um estado de direito democrático, prova disso mais uma vez, o ganancioso após o PR ter depositado coroas de flores no túmulo de ALC no dia dos heróis nacionais, reuniu os seus "gangs" para o mesmo efeito, conseguiu até mobilizar um dos familiares do Pai da Nação para lhe acompanhar tudo isso para manipular e dividir os guineenses "guineenses ku udjus fitchadu" para os seus intereses obscuros.

data.title: Guyana dreigt gasexportplannen te moeten halveren door behoefte ExxonMobil
data.description: Guyana overweegt zijn plannen voor de export van vloeibaar aardgas fors terug te schroeven. ExxonMobil verwacht dagelijks ongeveer 2 miljard kubieke voet gas nodig te hebben voor de olieproductie. Daardoor kan een gepland LNG-project met een capaciteit van 6 miljoen ton per jaar mogelijk worden gehalveerd. De Guyanese regering heeft nog geen definitief besluit genomen. The post Guyana dreigt gasexportplannen te moeten halveren door behoefte ExxonMobil appeared first on Suriname Herald .
